description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06) by a #1224 edge probe.  PRE-EXISTING; nothing
in the s470 batches moved it.  NOT FIXED HERE (out of the brief's scope).

MEASURED, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL (probe scratch/s470bv/p-edge2.pl row J):

    my $FH;
    my $ok = open($FH, "<", "/nonexistent-bv-$$") ? 1 : 0;
    printf "J failed open: ok=%s defined(\$FH)=%s\n", $ok, (defined $FH ? 1 : 0);

    perl : J failed open: ok=0 defined($FH)=1
    PCL  : J failed open: ok=0 defined($FH)=0

perl autovivifies the lexical into a fresh GLOB *before* it tries the open, so
the handle exists (and is a closed handle) whatever the open does; PCL only
writes the variable on success.

WHY IT MATTERS.  The idiom

    open(my $fh, "<", $f) or do { ... };
    ...
    close $fh if defined $fh;

and, more sharply, code that tests `defined $fh` to decide whether it owns a
handle, take the wrong branch under PCL.  It is a SILENT divergence: no
warning, no die, just a different boolean.

FIX (sketch, not attempted).  The `open` lowering writes its first argument
with the new handle; the write must happen on the FAILING path too, with a
closed handle object.  Look at `%p-open-impl`'s callers in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
(the lexical-handle arm) -- the handle object is already constructed before the
underlying open is attempted in the success path, so the change is to hoist
that construction and store it unconditionally, leaving it CLOSED when the
open fails.  Two things to keep: `open` still returns false, and `$!` still
carries the errno #1224 now sets.

ACCEPTANCE: the probe row prints `ok=0 defined($FH)=1`; a `Pl/t` guard row in
io-layers-01.t (or a new io-*-01.t) asserting both halves; and
`print {$fh} "x"` on the failed handle must fail the way perl's does
(print on a closed filehandle), not crash -- probe that before writing the fix.
=== DONE (s471a) ===
FIXED, own commit, runtime-only.

THE REPRESENTATION ALREADY EXISTED, and measuring that turned a design question
into a five-line fix: `Symbol::gensym` + a failed open ALREADY answered exactly
like perl in PCL (`defined` 1, `ref` GLOB, probe K06), so the only missing piece
was the autovivification itself.  `%p-autoviv-failed-handle` builds the glob ref
through `p-backslash`'s typeglob arm -- the ONE construction that sets `is-ref`,
which is what makes ref($fh) answer GLOB rather than "" -- and %p-open-impl's
failure arm calls it beside the %pcl-save-errno it already did.  open still
returns false and $! still carries #1224's errno.

ONLY AN UNDEF BOX autovivifies; the negatives are probed: a box holding a STRING
is perl's symbolic-filehandle spelling and keeps its value (`my $fh = "preset"`
stays "preset"); a box holding a glob is already the handle; a BAREWORD handle
is a symbol, not a box.  The anonymous globs carry uniqueness in their NAME
(Symbol::__PCL_ANONFH_<n>) because %p-resolve-fh's typeglob fallback compares
symbol NAMES across packages.

MEASURED, 24 one-file probes vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s471a/p1271, p1271b):
11 of 12 J-rows and 10 of 12 K-rows identical, up from 5 and 7.  defined, ref,
truthiness, stringification, ref(\$fh), copying and the RETRY
(`open($fh,â¦)` after a failure) all match now; fileno, <$fh>, print {$fh}, eof,
binmode already did and are unchanged.

BARS: gate 213/7347 (only the 13 xs rows); full sweep --jobs 4 GATE clean,
0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL 18647 (+0), drops 5 = census; the io/ companion
leg 44 files, whose only two differences were MEASURED PRE-EXISTING on an
ed302e13 extraction (io/perlio_fail.t stale at 6/9 vs 11/4 on both trees --
spliced; io/pvbm.t the documented flapper -- left alone).  Guard
Pl/t/io-layers-01.t 36 -> 38 rows (6.3 s wall), INVERSE-VERIFIED: both fail on
an ed302e13 extraction.

RESIDUE FILED, all three PRE-EXISTING and none caused or hidden by this change:
#1307 (`close` on a never-opened handle: perl's DEFINED "" vs PCL's undef),
#1308 (a SUCCESSFUL `open my $fh` leaves ref($fh) = "" -- the success path
box-sets the raw stream), #1309 (`open($a[0],â¦)` succeeds but `<$a[0]>` reads
nothing -- broken on the success path too, probed).
subject: A FAILED `open(my $fh, ...)` leaves $fh undef where perl autovivifies the glob: `defined($fh)` is 1 in perl and 0 in PCL after the open returns false
